claims.text: High-entropy alloy coatings with optimized composition can protect hot-dip aluminum plating equipment from erosion by liquid aluminum.
Optimizing the composition of high-entropy alloy coatings will improve resistance to liquid-aluminum corrosion.
Alloying elements are the structural mediator responsible for the proposed protection.
Alloying elements enhance the coating's corrosion resistance.
The proposed coatings will reduce corrosion rate by 50% relative to current materials.
The proposed material is intended to operate in contact with liquid aluminum at high temperature.
The exact high-entropy-alloy composition and optimal coating thickness are unknown.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a 50% corrosion-rate reduction, but the falsification rule accepts any reduction of at least 30%; therefore, an observed 30–49% reduction would fail the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
